resolutions.researcher_notes: Replaced the DEAD_LINK 2025 Arabic refs. Chevron greenlit CONSTRUCTION of the Nitzana line on 16 Sep 2025 (JPT/SPE 'Chevron Greenlights Construction'; Construction Review 'to Construct'); attaqa (Arabic energy trade) corroborates 'بدء أعمال بناء' with works launching Q4 2025 and ~3-yr build to ~2028. Independent en+ar origins. FLAG: status is greenlit/contracted with ground-breaking at Q4 2025, so 'construction' is defensible but at the leading edge; MEES (30 May 2025, paywalled, not cited) had reported a Nitzana 'setback' that could affect schedule.

ProposalYear=2023 supported by the May-2023 Israeli cabinet/government approval: MEES 2023-05-12 'Advances With Cabinet Approval', Enerdata (approved by the Israeli government in 2023), and the Israeli Ministry of Energy page (energy-sea.gov.il 'approved by government'). CONTRADICTION/NUANCE: the onshore line was first publicly floated Oct 2021 (Reuters exclusive / Offshore Technology / Pipeline Journal); 2021 is the first-proposal year and 2023 the formal government-approval year — 2023 is defensible but confirm which milestone ProposalYear intends.

DelayType='inferred' — no source explicitly labels the project 'delayed', consistent with an inferred (not sourced) value, so no ref added (avoids an orphan ref on a purely inferential value). The inference is supported by timeline slippage: Offshore Technology (2021) said it would be 'commissioned within 24 months' (~2023), whereas current reporting (JPT/SPE, Enerdata) puts construction start at Q4 2025 and completion ~2028; MEES (30 May 2025, paywalled) also reported a Nitzana 'setback'. Left UNRESOLVED because no verifiable source directly asserts a delay.

LengthKnown=65 km confirmed by JPT/SPE ('65 km, Ramat Hovav to Nitzana'), attaqa ('65 كيلومترًا') and safha1 (headline 'بطول 65 كيلو متر'). Three independent en+ar sources agree exactly. Minor FLAG: some reporting describes a '36-in., ~67-km' line (65-vs-67 km discrepancy) — 65 km is the better-corroborated figure.

FuelSource=Leviathan, Tamar confirmed. 2021 sources (Offshore Technology, Pipeline Journal) cite exports 'from Tamar and Leviathan offshore gas fields'. Rigzone (Oct 2025, independent of the 2021 wire) reports the line's capacity allocation as Leviathan 41.8% + Tamar 41.8% + Energean 16.4% — so BOTH Leviathan and Tamar remain major shippers (Tamar is NOT de-emphasized). ADDITION FLAG: Energean (Katlan field, ~2027) is now a third shipper the GEM value omits — consider adding Energean/Katlan to FuelSource.

StartLocation=Ramat Hovav (Negev, Israel), EndPrefecture=Nitzana at the Egyptian border. JPT/SPE: 'from Ramat Hovav industrial zone in the Negev to Nitzana at the Egyptian border'; attaqa: 'من رامات حوفاف في صحراء النقب إلى نيتسانا المنطقة الحدودية مع مصر'. Independent en+ar, exact match. NUANCE: Nitzana is the border crossing on the Israeli side into Egypt — GEM's EndCountryOrArea=Egypt reflects the destination/crossing, consistent with the onshore Israel→Egypt framing.

SegmentCost=$200,000,000 USD reflects the ORIGINAL 2021 estimate — Offshore Technology ('$200m pipeline') and Pipeline Journal ('$200 million-worth'). These two are NOT independent (both trace to the Oct-2021 Reuters exclusive), hence medium. CONTRADICTION FLAG: current figures are far higher — the Chevron/Leviathan-partners transportation deal with INGL is ~$610m (Times of Israel, JPT), the Israeli line was announced at ~NIS 2 billion, and Egypt is investing ~$400m on its side; MEES (2023) put the route at ~$245m ($350m incl. compressor). The $200M value is stale — recommend Update review before treating as current.

ToI (22 Feb 2021): Israeli and Egyptian energy ministers 'agreed Sunday to build a gas pipeline' from the offshore Leviathan platform to Egypt. WorldOil (20 Feb 2021): the two states 'may build' the undersea line and 'would work on a governmental framework' — i.e. an agreed-but-not-yet-built proposal, consistent with Status=proposed. Reuters (21 Oct 2021) frames a second subsea line to Egypt as still under consideration. Two independent originals support proposed.
Both describe a natural-gas pipeline carrying Leviathan/Tamar gas to Egypt. Fuel=Gas is uncontested across every source found.

ToI dated 22 Feb 2021 reports the just-announced agreement; WorldOil dated 20 Feb 2021 reports the same announcement. The proposal originates in Feb 2021, supporting ProposalYear=2021. Two independent originals.

CONTRADICTION FLAG: no source states the literal 6.70 bcm/y, but two independent sources bracket/support it. MEES (11 Mar 2022) describes this exact project — a cut-price pipeline delivering '6-7 bcm/year' direct to Egypt from Leviathan (verified: page contains 'Leviathan' and the '6-7' bcm figure). Offshore-Energy (20 Jan 2021, tracing to Delek Drilling) says the partners' new pipeline system will 'send as much as 7 billion cubic meters of gas annually to Egypt' (verified). 6.70 sits inside the 6-7 range and just below the 7 bcm ceiling. Outlier: Enerdata (11 Mar 2021) says the government-backed subsea project has '10 bcm/year capacity' that would 'double' Israel's export capacity to Egypt — likely a max/design figure vs the 6-7 bcm contracted throughput. Recommend Update confirm whether 6.70 is a throughput or design figure; the 6-7 bcm range is the best real support and the two cited sources are independent origins.

Both name the Leviathan and Tamar offshore reservoirs as the gas source feeding the Egypt export line; Reuters (Wayback) likewise cites 'Tamar and Leviathan offshore gas fields'. Note ToI frames the direct-from-rig pipeline as sourced primarily at Leviathan, with Tamar the associated smaller field. FuelSource well supported.

Both describe an (off/undersea) pipeline running from Israel's offshore Leviathan platform to Egypt, supporting StartCountryOrArea=Israel, EndCountryOrArea=Egypt. Only country-level endpoints are populated in the brief; no finer start/end place is asserted, and none is contradicted.

Status 'proposed' well supported. Pipeline Technology Journal (2025): project only in seabed-survey phase, was frozen in 2019 and reactivated by a Feb-2025 MoU. AP News and Asharq/Bloomberg (2025 Wayback) describe it as a still-to-be-built plan Egypt 'seeks' to realize. No construction begun and FID not taken as of 2026 (see FID unit). The stale prior current_ref (Reuters 2023) was a 401 bot-wall; replaced with three live independent sources.

values.Background: the company responsible for the project, Chevron wanted to send the gas to Egypt through a pipeline, but Cyprus preferred to process it on a floating production facility because it would be more economically beneficial for the Cypriot government and would lend more flexibility to supplying other markets.

resolutions.primary_value: the company responsible for the project, Chevron wanted to send the gas to Egypt through a pipeline, but Cyprus preferred to process it on a floating production facility because it would be more economically beneficial for the Cypriot government and would lend more flexibility to supplying other markets.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Background claim directly corroborated by two independent sources. Cyprus Mail (Dec 2023): the sticking point was the floating production unit (FPU) — Chevron wanted it scrapped and the field connected to Egyptian liquefaction via a subsea pipeline (saving ~EUR1bn), while Cyprus pushed for the FPU because it allows greater gas recovery and maximises Republic revenue. World Pipelines (Sep 2023) frames the same subsea-pipeline vs FPU dispute. Matches the value's substance (Chevron=pipeline, Cyprus=FPU for economic benefit).

ProposalYear 2018 confirmed by two independent sources. Reuters (7 May 2018, via Wayback) reports El Molla/Lakkotrypis agreeing to the Aphrodite-to-Egypt pipeline plan. Oil & Gas Journal reports the Cyprus-Egypt intergovernmental agreement signed 20 Sep 2018. Working ref is the Wayback snapshot of the 2018 Reuters article (original uk.reuters.com URL is dead).

CONTRADICTION FLAG. StartYear1 2028 traces to Asharq/Bloomberg (Jul 2025, headline 'Egypt seeks ~1.3 bcf of Cypriot gas by end of 2028'), and the original attaqa.net current_ref was a broken/mismatched URL (200 but wrong article). However, more recent 2026 reporting contradicts 2028: worldoil.com, EnterpriseAM and Bloomberg (Apr-Jun 2026) put pipeline construction ~2027 and first gas ~2030 (some to 2031). 2028 is a single 2025 target now likely stale; recommend Update review toward 2030.

Capacity 8 bcm/y supported by About Energy (eni World Energy magazine, Jul 2019, via Wayback): 'an underwater 240-to-320 km gas pipeline to deliver around 8 billion cubic meters (bcm) of gas a year to Egypt.' Single strong independent source; no second source found stating 8 bcm precisely (later coverage cites up to 700 mmcf/d ~ 7.2 bcm/y). Medium.

PARTIAL SUPPORT. About Energy (eni, Jul 2019) gives the length as an 'underwater 240-to-320 km gas pipeline' (intro says '300 km'). LengthKnown 310 km falls inside that range and is consistent with '300 km', but no source states exactly 310 km. One other search hit cited a 170 km line. Low — value plausible but not pinned to a precise independent figure.

CONTRADICTION FLAG on end terminal. Start point (Aphrodite field, Cyprus) and country pair (Cyprus->Egypt) firmly corroborated by Reuters 2018 and About Energy 2019. BUT the specific end terminal is disputed: About Energy and NS Energy Business both say the destination is the Idku LNG terminal near Alexandria, NOT Damietta. Reuters 2018 says only 'Egypt's LNG facilities.' EndLocation 'Damietta Segas LNG Terminal' is not independently corroborated and may be a GEM interpretation; recent 2026 deals route gas to Port Said/grid. Recommend Update review of EndLocation.

SegmentCost $1bn USD supported by two independent sources. Reuters (7 May 2018, El Molla): pipeline 'will cost between $800 million and $1 billion' — value takes the upper bound. About Energy (2019, Lakkotrypis): 'initial estimate is around USD1 billion.' Note newer 2025 reporting (Financial Mirror) escalates the figure to ~$2bn; the $1bn value reflects the 2018-19 estimate.

FIDStatus 'Pre-FID' confirmed: EnterpriseAM (Jun 2026) reports the Egyptian Oil Ministry is still 'pushing for a September FID' on the Aphrodite field — i.e. FID not yet taken. Pipeline Technology Journal (2025) shows the project only at seabed-survey/FEED stage. Consistent with a not-yet-sanctioned project.

Original Asharq Business link (seed/current ref) is dead (HTTP 202); replaced with the 2025-07-30 Wayback snapshot, which verifies 200 + content. Asharq (29 Jul 2025, citing two Egyptian officials): Eni 'targets completing a 90 km subsea pipeline to transport gas to the onshore processing plant in Port Said in 2027', with FID/agreements still pending. egyptoil-gas (independent) corroborates: FID expected 2025, marine surveys underway 'for the planned gas pipeline route'. Not yet built/FID'd -> proposed. Two independent sources agree the project is pre-construction.
Both sources describe the line as carrying natural gas (الغاز) from the Cronos gas field to Egypt. Fuel = Gas fully supported by 2 independent sources.

Asharq describes a dedicated subsea trunkline (خط أنابيب بحري) that carries Cronos field gas to the onshore processing plant and feeds part of the output into Egypt's national gas grid -> a transmission (not gathering/distribution) line. 'transmission' is a GEM classification not stated verbatim, but the described function (long-distance field-to-grid trunk) supports it. Single-source; medium.

Asharq: completing the 90 km line and connecting 500 mmcf/d from Cronos 'by the end of 2027' (بنهاية 2027). MEES (independent) states connection targeted 'before the end of 2027'. StartYear1=2027 supported by 2 independent sources. Caveat: both note FID pending and flag 2028 as the more realistic fallback, but the stated target year is 2027.

Asharq: 'ربط 500 مليون قدم مكعب يومياً من حقل كرونوس' (connecting 500 million cubic feet/day from the Cronos field). MEES (independent, in English): 'around 500mn cfd of output will be sent ... to Eni's Zohr facilities'. Capacity=500 MMcf/d supported by 2 independent sources.

Asharq explicitly states 'خط أنابيب بحري بطول 90 كيلومتراً' (a 90 km subsea pipeline) to the onshore Port Said processing plant -> LengthKnown=90 km directly supported. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: MEES describes ~'70km southeast to Eni's Zohr facilities' — a shorter figure measured to the offshore Zohr facilities rather than to the onshore Port Said plant. The 90 km value (line to onshore Port Said) rests on a single source; medium.

Asharq: subsea line from the Cronos field (offshore southwest Cyprus) to the onshore processing plant 'in Port Said' (في بورسعيد) -> StartCountryOrArea=Cyprus, EndState/Province=Port Said, End=Egypt. egyptoil-gas (independent) corroborates the Cronos->Egypt route and references Port Said processing facilities. Note: GEM's EndCountryOrArea is spelled 'Egypy' (typo) — should read 'Egypt'; flagging for correction, not a sourcing issue.

Value 'proposed' supported: as of Sept 2025 Israel's Energy Ministry approved the pipeline and Chevron/INGL signed the EPC/build agreement, but construction was only scheduled to begin end-2025 with commissioning 2028 — i.e. announced/pre-construction, consistent with 'proposed'. ENR and Times of Israel are independent (trade press vs Israeli outlet) and both describe a newly-agreed, not-yet-built line. No contradiction to the stated value.

Value 'Gas' fully supported: both sources describe the Nitzana line as a natural-gas export pipeline carrying Leviathan-field gas from the Negev/Ramat Hovav to the Nitzana crossing into Egypt. Two independent outlets; no contradiction.

Value 'transmission' supported: the project is governed by a 'Transmission Agreement' with Israel Natural Gas Lines (verified token 'Transmission' present in both ENR and Rigzone). Physically a ~65-67 km long-distance export trunk with a new compressor station moving ~600 mmcfd cross-border — a transmission (not gathering/distribution) line by both label and function. Two independent sources; no contradiction to the value.

Value 610,000,000 USD supported: both sources state a $610 million deal between Chevron and INGL to build the Nitzana pipeline (Times of Israel headline: '$610m deal'; ENR: '$610M Nitzana Pipeline'). Note the $610M is the Israeli-side EPC/build figure; Egypt separately invests ~$400M on its own side (via Gasco) — the GEM SegmentCost captures the $610M Israeli-side value only. Two independent sources agree; no contradiction.

Original ref (petroleumfuture.net/28363) is dead (ConnectionError; no Wayback copy). Replaced. Status=construction well supported by two independent Egyptian outlets citing separate official-gazette decrees: (1) almasdar.com reports Ministry of Petroleum decree 1883/2025, Official Gazette issue 283-'د' dated 16 Dec 2025 — 'الموافقة على تنفيذ مشروع خط غاز السليمانية - شمال الجيزة' (approval to EXECUTE the project); (2) dostor.org reports Giza governorate decree 297/2026 (Apr 2026) temporarily seizing the route land for 3 years to build the line + 3 valve rooms. Ministerial execution approval + active land-seizure for construction = project in construction. No contradiction.
Fuel=Gas. Both sources name it 'خط غاز السليمانية – شمال الجيزة' (Solaimaneyah–North Giza GAS pipeline); GASCO (جاسكو) national natural-gas network trunk. Unambiguous.

PipelineType=transmission. Supported indirectly but strongly: a 42-inch (قطر 42 بوصة) GASCO trunk feeding/reinforcing the national natural-gas network (الشبكة القومية للغازات الطبيعية) with 3 valve rooms (غرف بلوف) — this is a high-pressure transmission line, not distribution. Sources do not use the literal word 'transmission' but the diameter/operator/valve-station profile is transmission-class.
Diameter=42 in. Both sources explicitly state 'قطر 42 بوصة' (diameter 42 inches). Two independent outlets citing separate official decrees agree. High confidence.

Route = Solaimaneyah (السليمانية) → North Giza (شمال الجيزة), both within Giza governorate (محافظة الجيزة), Egypt; ~20 km ('بطول 20 كم'). Both sources name it 'خط غاز السليمانية – شمال الجيزة' and place the entire route inside Giza governorate. FLAG: sheet EndLocation is recorded as 'Giza' — the decree endpoint is specifically 'North Giza' (شمال الجيزة, i.e. Giza North power-plant area); consider setting EndLocation='North Giza' for precision. StartLocation/State and country all corroborated.

Status = construction confirmed. Vetogate (Ministry of Petroleum Decision 1884/2025) describes the 3-pipeline New Fayoum gas project as under construction on an 18-month timeline, with the main supply line and valve room #3 already implemented. El-Muashir independently reports the project being executed by Fayoum Gas Company, technical study finished, main feed line implemented and pressure chamber #3 completed. Masrawy (GASCO 2024) and dostor (dostor.org/4519815, GASCO 2023 accomplishments, mentions 'خط تغذية توسعات مدينة الفيوم الجديدة') also corroborate active execution. Two independent origins agree -> high. Original GEM refs (petroleumfuture.net/28363, elfagr.org/5133728) are dead/403; petroleumfuture article survives as a working mirror at elmostqpalelyuom.com/28363.

LengthKnown = 40 km confirmed. Masrawy (GASCO 2024): 'مشروع خطوط تغذية الفيوم الجديدة ومدينة أطسا وتدعيم الفيوم القديمة بإجمالى أطوال 40 كم' (New Fayoum + Atsa + Old Fayoum support feed lines, total 40 km) — same figure verbatim in elmostqpalelyuom.com/28363. Vetogate gives 40.5 km for the three-line project. Two independent origins agree within rounding -> high. Note the 40 km is the combined length of the 3-pipe family serving New Fayoum, Atsa and Old Fayoum, matching the single GEM row.

Diameter = 16,24 in confirmed by a single strong source. Vetogate (Ministry Decision 1884/2025) states the pipelines are 24-inch and 16-inch, operating at 70 bar. No independent second source found for the diameters specifically: masrawy/elmostqpalelyuom cite 42-inch and 36-inch only for other (Suleimaniya-North Giza, Tina-Mit Nama, Trans-Sinai) lines, not the Fayoum line. Single strong -> medium.

StartLocation = New Fayoum City (الفيوم الجديدة), Fayoum governorate, Egypt confirmed by multiple independent sources (vetogate, masrawy, elmuashir, dostor). CONTRADICTION TO FLAG on start/end direction: GEM lists New Fayoum City as StartLocation, but vetogate states the pipeline ORIGINATES in Beni Suef governorate and extends westward, TERMINATING at New Fayoum City — i.e. New Fayoum reads as the endpoint, not the start, and a Beni Suef start-point (currently blank in GEM) is implied. Also the line serves Atsa (أطسا/إطسا) and Old Fayoum in addition to New Fayoum. Location value itself is well-supported; suggest human review of start/end assignment against the routes repo.

Owner1=Israel Natural Gas Lines (INGL) 100% confirmed. Offshore Technology & Pipeline Journal (2021): 'owned by Israel Natural Gas Lines'. JPT/SPE (2025, independent): INGL will construct, operate and manage the line under a 15-year extendable contract. The 2021 pair traces to Reuters, but the 2025 JPT source is independent and agrees. NOTE: the Leviathan upstream partners (Chevron ~40%, NewMed, Ratio) fund/contract the line as shippers/capacity holders but INGL is the pipeline owner-operator.

Owner1 = Israel Natural Gas Lines (100%). Reuters (Wayback capture of the paywalled 21 Oct 2021 exclusive; live reuters.com 401s under url_verifier): 'The pipeline will be owned by Israeli national distribution company Israel Natural Gas Lines.' Offshore-Energy (20 Jan 2021) independently states Chevron 'entered into an agreement with Israel Natural Gas Lines (INGL) for the provision of transmission services' for the Egypt export line. Two independent origins name INGL; INGL is Israel's state gas-transmission monopoly, so 100% Israel-side ownership is consistent. CAVEAT: contemporaneous 2021 coverage partly conflates the offshore/subsea concept with a companion onshore route; I did not find a source explicitly restricting INGL ownership to the offshore variant alone, but no source contradicts it. (Corrected from a prior draft that cited Enerdata for INGL — the Enerdata article does not actually name INGL.)

Legacy ownership Noble Energy 35% / Shell 35% / Delek Drilling 30% confirmed by three independent sources (Offshore Technology, NS Energy, About Energy). UPDATE FLAG: this is the pre-2020 structure. Chevron bought Noble Energy in Oct 2020 and is now operator with 35%; Shell holds 35% and NewMed Energy (formerly Delek) 30%. The sheet's Owner2 'Noble Energy' and Owner3 'Delek Group' are outdated — current holders are Chevron and NewMed. Recommend Update refresh of owner entities.
